title: 3.5.15 Lab: Add a Method to an Object
description: Give an object a method, call it, and print its return value. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Build an object with data
steps.instructions: Create a variable called student holding an object literal with at least one data property, such as a name.

steps.title: Add a method
steps.instructions: Add a property whose value is a function. Give it a clear name and have it return a string.

steps.title: Call the method
steps.instructions: Call the method with parentheses and print what it returns.

requirements.title: method defined on the object
requirements.description: A property is assigned a function. Help: 3.5.13 (Methods)
requirements.hint: A method is a property whose value is a function. Write the property name, a colon, then the function.

requirements.title: method called with parentheses
requirements.hint: Call it the way you read a property, but add parentheses after the name: the object, a dot, the method, then ( ).

requirements.title: return used
requirements.description: The method hands a value back. Help: 3.5.13 (Methods)
requirements.hint: A method that hands a value back needs the word return followed by the value.

requirements.title: result printed
requirements.hint: Wrap the call in console.log so the returned value shows up in the output.

requirements.title: the method returns a value that is printed
requirements.description: student has a method, and the output shows what that method returns. Help: 3.5.13 (Methods)
requirements.hint: A method that returns nothing prints undefined. Have the function return a string, call it with parentheses and print the result.

checks.expr: student !== null && typeof student === 'object' && output.length >= 1 && output.every(l => l.trim() !== '' && l.trim() !== 'undefined') && Object.values(student).some(f => typeof f === 'function' && (() => { try { return output.some(l => l.includes(String(f.call(student)))); } catch (e) { return false; } })())
checks.fail: student needs a method that returns a string, and you must print what it returns: console.log(student.methodName()).
